**CuraLit Project Team** • Biomedical Research • AI/ML • Literature Mining

# Abstract

**CuraLit** transforms how researchers interact with scientific literature by enabling the creation of **custom AI assistants** trained on curated PubMed articles. This Rust-based tool filters millions of articles by keywords, generates comprehensive statistics and visualizations, and produces specialized Large Language Models (LLMs) using Ollama. Unlike generic AI assistants, CuraLit creates domain-specific experts that can answer questions, synthesize findings, and identify research gaps from your selected corpus. **Key advantages**: memory-efficient processing, resumable operations, interactive visualizations, and easy model sharing. Perfect for literature reviews, grant writing, hypothesis generation, and team collaboration.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## 🎯 Core Innovation
Transform **36+ million PubMed articles** → **Focused corpus** → **Custom AI research assistant** in minutes!
:::
:::

::: {style="background: lightyellow; padding: 1.5rem; border-radius: 8px; margin-bottom: 2rem;"}

# System Architecture

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
## Components & Features

**1. Search Engine**
- Streaming XML parser (memory-efficient)
- Keyword matching (AND/OR logic)
- Checkpoint system (resumable)
- Parallel processing with Rayon

**2. Analytics & Visualizations**
- Comprehensive statistical analysis
- MeSH term extraction & ranking
- Author/journal distribution analysis
- Interactive Plotly/Seaborn dashboards
- Publication timeline trends

**3. AI Model Generation**
- Ollama Modelfile creation
- JSONL training data export
- Custom system prompts
- Multiple base models: llama3, mistral, phi3

**4. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)** 🆕
- Vector database with Qdrant
- Embedding via nomic-embed-text
- Citation-backed answers with PMIDs
- No hallucination - facts retrieved directly

**5. Database Fact Verification** 🆕 v0.3.3
- SQLite database with FTS5 search
- Automatic PMID verification
- Prevent AI citation hallucination
- Fast indexed lookups (<1ms)
:::

# Use Cases

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="32%"}
## 📚 Literature Reviews

**Challenge**: Synthesize 200+ papers for PhD thesis

**Solution**:
```bash
curalit search \
  -k "immunotherapy" \
  -k "cancer treatment" \
  -d ./pubmed_data \
  -o thesis_review
```

**Benefits**:
- Automated article filtering
- Statistical overvi48%"}
## 📚 Literature Reviews & Grant Writing

**Challenge**: Synthesize 200+ papers for PhD thesis or NSF proposal

**Solution**:
```bash
# Search & filter relevant articles
curalit search \
  -k "immunotherapy" \
  -k "cancer treatment" \
  -d ./pubmed_data \
  -o thesis_review

# Build knowledge base with RAG
curalit rag-build -c thesis_review.csv

# Build verification database
curalit db-build \
  -k "immunotherapy" \
  -k "cancer treatment" \
  -d ./pubmed_data \
  -n thesis_db

# Query with verified citations
curalit rag-generate \
  -q "What are the mechanisms?" \
  -m llama3 \
  --use-db 0_out/thesis_db.db
```

**Benefits**:
✅ Automated article filtering (minutes vs hours)  
✅ Statistical overview with visualizations  
✅ AI Q&A on findings with citations  
✅ **Verified references** - no hallucination!  
✅ Gap identification for hypothesis  

**Result**: Weeks → Days of work
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
## 👥 Team Collaboration & Clinical Practice

**Challenge**: Lab needs shared knowledge base; Doctors need current research

**Solution**:
```bash
# Create comprehensive model
curalit search \
  -f lab_keywords.txt \
  -d ./data \
  -o lab_knowledge

# Generate & package for team
curalit generate \
  -c lab_knowledge.csv \
  -m lab-assistant \
  --package

# Package RAG model with database
curalit rag-package \
  -n lab_articles \
  -o lab_rag_model
```

**Team Uses**:
- Onboard new lab members quickly
- Answer common research questions
- Standardize knowledge across team
- Support experimental design decisions
- **Evidence-based answers** with PMIDs

**Ask Model**:
- "What are recent breakthroughs?"
- "What gaps exist in our field?"
- "Who are leading researchers?"
- "What are recommended protocols?"

**Result**: Consistent expertise, better patient communication
:::
::::
y Advantages**:
✅ No hallucination  
✅ Auto-citations (PMIDs)  
✅ Fast setup (minutes)  
✅ Easy updates  
✅ Small packages (~MB)
:::

::: {.column width="35%"}
**RAG Workflow**

```bash
# 1. Start vector database
docker run -d --name curalit-qdrant \
  -p 6333:6333 -p 6334:6334 \
  qdrant/qdrant

# 2. Install embedding model
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

# 3. Build RAG index
curalit rag-build -c results.csv

# 4. Query knowledge base
curalit rag-query \
  -q "What are the mechanisms?"

# 5. Generate answers
curalit rag-generate \
  -q "Compare treatments" \
  -m llama3
```
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
**RAG vs Fine-tuning**

| Feature | RAG | Fine-tune |
|---------|-----|-----------|
| Accuracy | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐ |
| Speed | ⚡⚡⚡ | ⚡ |
| Citations | ✅ | ❌ |
| Updates | Easy | Hard |

**Sharing RAG Models**:
```bash
# Package with vector DB
curalit rag-package \
  -n curalit_articles \
  -o research_rag

# Recipients:
# 1. Extract archive
# 2. Run ./setup_rag.sh
# 3. Start querying!
```

**Best for**: Fact-based Q&A, literature review, research queries
:::

# Quick Start Guide

## Installation (5 minutes)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Prerequisites**
```bash
# Install Rust
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 \
  -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh

# Install Ollama
# Visit: ollama.ai/download

# Install UV (Python package manager)
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
# Or: pip install uv
```
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
**Build CuraLit**
```bash
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/\
  yourusername/curalit.git
cd curalit

# Build release version
cargo build --release

# Test installation
./target/release/curalit --version
# Output: curalit 0.2.0
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note}
UV automatically manages all Python dependencies from pyproject.toml - no manual package installation needed!
:::

## Complete Workflow Example

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Steps 1-2: Search & Analyze**
```bash
# Step 1: Search
curalit search \
  -k "diabetes" \
  -k "treatment" \
  -d ./data \
  -o diabetes_study

# Step 2: Analyze
curalit stats -c diabetes_study.csv
```

**Output**: 
- CSV with matching articles (⏱️ 2-5 min)
- JSON statistics & analysis report (⏱️ 10 sec)

**Steps 3-4: Visualize & Generate**
```bash
# Step 3: Visualize
uv run diabetes_study_visualize.py

# Step 4: Generate model
curalit generate \
  -c diabetes_study.csv \
  -m diabetes-expert \
  -b llama3 --package
```

**Output**: 
- Interactive HTML dashboards (⏱️ 30 sec)
- Modelfile + training data + package (⏱️ 5-10 min)
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
**Alternative: RAG + Database Workflow** 🆕
```bash
# Build RAG index for Q&A
curalit rag-build -c diabetes_study.csv

# Build database for verification
curalit db-build \
  -k "diabetes" -k "treatment" \
  -d ./data -n diabetes_db

# Query with verified citations
curalit rag-generate \
  -q "Latest diabetes treatments?" \
  -m llama3 \
  --use-db 0_out/diabetes_db.db
```

**OR: Traditional Fine-tuning**
```bash
# Create the model
ollama create diabetes-expert \
  -f Modelfile_diabetes-expert_*

# Run interactive session
ollama run diabetes-expert

>>> What are the latest treatment 
    approaches for type 2 diabetes?

Based on 247 articles (2018-2024):
1. GLP-1 receptor agonists (PMID: 32456789)
2. SGLT2 inhibitors (PMID: 31234567)
3. CGM for personalized care (PMID: 33567890)
...
```
:::

## Benchmark Performance

| Dataset Size | Processing Time | Memory Usage |
|--------------|----------------|--------------|
| 100K articles | 45 seconds | 250 MB |

| 1M articles | 7 minutes | 320 MB |

**Key Metrics**:
- 📊 **Throughput**: ~2,400 articles/second
- 💾 **Memory**: Constant (~300MB regardless of size)
- 🔄 **Resumability**: 100% (checkpoint every 100 articles)

# Advanced Features

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
## Keyword Strategies

**AND Logic (Specific)**
```bash
curalit search \
  -k "CRISPR-Cas9" \
  -k "gene editing" \
  -k "therapeutic" \
  -d ./data & Distribution

**AND Logic (Specific)**
```bash
curalit search \
  -k "CRISPR-Cas9" \
  -k "gene editing" \
  -k "therapeutic" \
  -d ./data
# Result: 127 highly relevant articles
```

**OR Logic (Broad)**
```bash
curalit search \
  -k "diabetes" -k "glucose" \
  --logic OR -d ./data
# Result: 3,456 related articles
```

**From Keywords File**
```bash
# keywords.txt contains:
# cancer immunotherapy
# checkpoint inhibitors
# PD-1
# PD-L1

curalit search -f keywords.txt -d ./data
```

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Optimal Corpus Size"}
**50-500 articles**: Excellent model quality  
**500-1000 articles**: Good, may be slower  
**>1000 articles**: Too broad, refine keywords  
**<50 articles**: Too narrow, use OR logic
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
## Distribution Options

**1. Package Files (Recommended)**
```bash
curalit package -m my-model
# Creates: my-model_distributable.tar.gz
# Size: ~KB-MB (metadata only)
```

**2. RAG Package (With Vector DB)**
```bash
curalit rag-package -n curalit_articles \
  -o research_rag
# Creates: research_rag.tar.gz
# Includes: vector DB + config + setup script
```

**3. Ollama Registry (Public Sharing)**
```bash
ollama create my-model -f Modelfile_*
ollama tag my-model user/my-model
ollama push user/my-model
# Size: GB (full model weights)
```

**4. Database Export**
```bash
# Share SQLite database
cp 0_out/research_db.db shared/
# Recipients can query directly:
sqlite3 research_db.db \
  "SELECT * FROM articles WHERE pmid='12345';"
```

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
**Package Advantages**: Small size, offline, no account, version control friendly
:::

# Limitations & Future Work {.block fill="lightsalmon"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
## Current Limitations

**1. Data Source**
- Limited to PubMed XML format
- Requires manual data download
- No real-time updates

**2. Model Training**
- Uses base models (not true fine-tuning)
- Context window limited to base model
- No GPU optimization (yet)

**3. Language Support**
- English-focused
- Non-English articles may be missed

**4. Interface**
- Command-line only
- No graphical interface
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

## Getting Started

```bash
# 1. Install CuraLit
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/curalit.git
cargo build --release

# 2. Download PubMed data
wget ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/baseline/pubmed*.xml.gz

# 3. Run your first search
./target/release/curalit search -k "your topic" -d ./data

# 4. Generate your AI assistant
./target/release/curalit generate -c results.csv -m my-model
```
:::
